Hello goats, I have my CCP and often hit the range to practice on my carry weapon. I'm no competition shooter or anything but I'm getting to be a fairly accurate shot at 5yards. Here's my question:

Is there any safe way to prepare yourself for an actual situation? Whenever going to the range you take your time to put on eyes and ears - a luxury not often afforded when you need to use your concealed carry on an imminent threat. I know for a fact that after my first bullet I will flinch like hell reacting to my ears and eyes getting hit with the percussive blasts. Should I just keep banking on my first shot hitting? My first time shooting was out in the woods, I had ears but no eyes on and I really couldn't keep my eyes open to see where I hit.

Sorry if it's a stupid question but I'd like to hear how you goats prepare for real life vs shooting at the range.

You have to develop muscle memory that is independent of conscious thought. This should involve two types of training. The first is to exhaust yourself physically and then train with the weapon. Doing this makes the mind more receptive to conditioning. Try running 3 miles as fast as you can before each shooting range visit. The second part requires you to very methodically plan, organize, write down, and then practice every micro-step related to shooting. You need to identify your target, draw your weapon, remove the weapon's safety, squeezing the trigger 3 to 5 times, re-engaging the weapon's safety, returning the weapon to the holster, etc. However, turn what I just told you into 40 or more micro-steps and monotonously go through each step- every single time. Practice those micro-steps in order, over and over, until it begins to feel really weird if you miss any step or change the order of any micro-step. Then keep training that way until your brain no longer translates instructions and your body begins performing correct actions without thought.

Practice. Lots of practice. Do you draw from concealed to fire? Do you fire to empty and reload? Do you practice malfunction drills? Do you practice shooting while moving or firing from cover? Do you practice drawing, firing, moving to cover, clearing a malfunction, reloading, reengaging, and re-holstering? If you're genuinely concerned about being able to effectively handle your carry piece and its caliber under stress, you may want to practice with it more and/or consider a tamer round. What are you firing that has you so concerned about flinching?

Don't practice without ear pro. Ever. Tinnitus is forever, and it sucks, trust me on this one. If it's life or death, oh well. When you have the opportunity to use ear pro, though, not doing so is just bad all around.

Look around for a range that holds practical shooting competitions. It'll get you off the couch on a Saturday and drop you into something different from a static paper silhouette on a firing lane. You'll be forced to move, fire from different positions, reload, and assess the targets. It will cause you to think on your feet, which is very useful in all aspects of life.

I'm getting a lot of tips on how to keep practicing, most of which I've already taken into consideration. My real quandary is when you will be shooting with no ear and eye protection, maybe even inside. I have found no advice geared towards this yet... Even if I had my .22, shooting indoors will just be different after the first round. When I say flinch I don't mean I would not hit the target, but I highly doubt I could maintain putting 10 rds in the bull at 15 ft without any protection
